classification.difficultyReason: Combine the two given angles to calculate the whole area, then recognise and formulate an additive-area equation for the two triangles sharing the unknown side before solving it.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with B lower left, C lower right, A above B, and D on AC. BD divides the angle at B into 45 degrees and 15 degrees. Ordinary outlines and labels use black; there is no shading.
spec.mathematics: AB=12, BC=20, BD=x, angle ABD=45 degrees and angle DBC=15 degrees. Coordinates use these givens and the intersection of the 15-degree ray with AC.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear; no calculated area, length or combined angle is printed.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence, find the value of $x$. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
Since $D$ lies on $AC$, the areas of $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle BCD$ add to the area of $\triangle ABC$.
$\begin{align*}60\sqrt3&=\tfrac12\times12x\sin45^\circ+\tfrac12\times20x\sin15^\circ\\60\sqrt3&=x(6\sin45^\circ+10\sin15^\circ)\\x&=\frac{60\sqrt3}{6\sin45^\circ+10\sin15^\circ}\\x&\approx15.2\end{align*}$
